title: ork show RUN [NAME]: print the pause reason, a role report and the check logs, with --json
lead: *Proposed.* An operator, or the agent acting for them, can read why a run is paused from ork itself. `ork show RUN` prints the run's state, the whole pause reason (and the owner question with its options when the pause is a question), the report files of each role attempt, the check results with their log names, and the owner and later findings with their full text. When the run is paused it also prints the pending role's newest report in full. `ork show RUN NAME` prints one named report (`reviewer-1-attempt-3.md`) or one check log (`checks-2.log`). Both forms take `--json`. No new file access is added for the caller: the daemon reads the run directory, as it already does for the TUI's report view (`run.report`, S176). The smallest design is one new read-only wire method (`run.show`), a small extension of `run.report` so it can serve check logs, and one CLI command. Owner decisions, 2026-11-05 (interactive interview, all recommended options): S281 stays a row until this slice lands, then is retired as done by it, and its findings are carried here (Q1 retire-s281); bare `ork show RUN` prints the summary, and when the run is paused also the pending role's newest report, otherwise only the report names (Q2 paused-report); `run.report` also serves a check log named in `checks[].log`, with the same guards (Q3 extend-run-report), which reverses S176's 2026-10-29 note ("no shell ork report; check logs out of scope") for the CLI; nothing else is served, no live tail and no other run file (Q4 reports-and-logs-only).
findings_note: 2026-11-05, prism-ui: run ork-20261105-173816-e0c2 (U32) paused on report shape; the reviewer's report could not be read through ork. ork status prints the pause reason and no findings; ork status --json carries run fields and roles[].report names but no report text, checks or pending role and round; ork help lists no command that prints a report. The only way was the file under ~/.local/state/ork/runs/RUN/, outside the folders a coding agent may read. The daemon already has run.report (S176) for the TUI; no CLI command calls it. Related: S281 (same title row, no slice yet), S176, S294, S295. Carried from S281 (owner decision 2026-11-05, Q1 retire-s281): Wave 7, 2026-11-04: steering paused runs meant reading run.json, report files and the grok fixture dir under ~/.local/state/ork by hand; ork status takes no run argument and prints a long wait reason and every denied command on one line; wanted the run state, whole pause reason or question with options, latest report per role, check results with logs, and denied commands as a count with the first few.
boundary: **Not in this slice:** the wording and layout of `ork status` (S240); `ork projects show` (S247); a command that changes state (retry, answer and stop stay as they are); any file outside a run's reports and check logs (raw vendor output, the live tail, the vendor fixture directory); a TUI change (the TUI already reads reports through `run.report`); fixing why a report fails its shape check (S298, S288).

sections.heading: Why
sections.body:
Owner evidence, 2026-11-05 (prism-ui; run `ork-20261105-173816-e0c2`, item U32): the run paused on report shape because the reviewer's `[owner]` findings did not parse (S298 has the cause). The operator could not see why. The facts below were read from the code at HEAD of main (`6a45b77`) and from `ork help` and `ork status` on 2026-11-05. I did not read the run directory under `~/.local/state/ork` and did not run any state-changing command.

- `ork status` has no report text. The CLI status handler (`internal/cli/daemoncmds.go:26-118`) prints, per run, `ID ITEM STATE`, then `(wait: REASON; next: ...)` (`:93-99`), the denials and a working line. It prints no findings and no roles. `ork status` also refuses a run argument (`:34-36`, "status takes no arguments").
- `ork status --json` is the daemon's `EngineRun` (`internal/source/source.go:241-279`). It has `id`, `item`, `branch`, `state`, `wait`, `pending` (the kind only, a string), `question` (the pending owner question when the kind is `question`), `roles[]` with the `report` file name (`source.go:167-182`) and `findings[]` with title and options but not the finding text (`source.go:189-198`). It has no `checks[]`, no pending role or round, no pending reason apart from `wait` (which has `; next: ork retry ID` appended, `internal/daemon/runs.go:1308-1322`) and no report text. The record holds more: `runrec.Finding.Text` (`internal/runrec/record.go:345-359`), `Checks []CheckRecord` with `Log` (`record.go:95-101`, `:296`) and `Pending.Role` and `Pending.Round` (`record.go:154-176`).
- `ork help` lists no command that prints a report (`internal/cli/cli.go:44`, `usageTemplate`; read through `ork help` output on 2026-11-05).
- The daemon already serves report text. `run.report` takes `{run,name}` and returns `{name,text}` (`internal/daemon/runs.go:1412-1416` and `:1436-1450`; wire name at `:40`; dispatch at `:1214`). The name must be one listed in the stored record's `roles[].report`; the file must be a regular `.md` file directly in the run directory, plain text, at most 64 KiB (`internal/engine/report.go:23-45`, the `.md` check is at `:29`). The Go client has `Client.Report` (`internal/daemon/client.go:210-214`); only the TUI calls it (`internal/tui/report.go`, `docs/design.md:1442-1456`, `docs/orchestrator-parity.md:113`). No CLI command calls it.
- A refused report is kept. A role's report name is stored on its role record when the attempt ends, before the shape check runs (`internal/engine/round.go:428-449`), and each attempt writes a distinct name: `ROLE-N.md` for attempt 1, `ROLE-N-attempt-A.md` after (`internal/engine/round.go:247-257`). So the report that failed the shape check is listed and `run.report` can already read it.
- A shape-failed report's findings are not recorded. `recordFindings` runs only when the shape check passes (`internal/engine/round.go:567-569`, `internal/engine/later.go:36-61`). So for a shape pause the report file is the only place the finding text exists.
- The check log is `checks-ROUND.log` (`internal/engine/states.go:224`), one per round, holding each command's output tail (30000 bytes per command, `internal/engine/states.go:213-221`) and `slicer check --json`. `checks[]` rows name it (`internal/engine/states.go:239`). That method does not serve it, because its name guard is the `roles[].report` list, and the file reader accepts only `.md` (`internal/engine/report.go:29`; `docs/orchestrator-parity.md:113` says raw logs are not exposed).
- `docs/state.md:16-17` lists both locations. The folder is outside what a coding agent may read, so without a CLI command the owner's agent cannot see a pause (the evidence case).

Check before specifying (AGENTS.md rule): slicer does not read ork's run directory. `slicer --root ../slicer find report` returned only unrelated items, and `find "show run"` and `find "pause reason"` (2026-11-05) returned none. Not verified beyond those searches.

An earlier owner decision touches this slice. S176's note of 2026-10-29 reads: "Owner decisions 2026-10-29 (interactive): defaults accepted (key p; no shell ork report; check logs out of scope)." That was S176's scope (the TUI viewer). This slice adds a shell command that prints reports and serves check logs, so it reverses both defaults for the CLI. Owner decision, 2026-11-05 (Q2 paused-report, Q3 extend-run-report): the CLI prints reports and serves check logs, reversing those two 2026-10-29 defaults for the CLI. The TUI viewer is unchanged.

Related: S281 is an open roadmap row, no slice yet, titled "ork show RUN: pause reason, question, latest report and checks in one command" (importance 3, urgency 3, effort 1). It asks for the same command and has no report-text requirement or design. This slice is its full spec. Owner decision, 2026-11-05 (Q1 retire-s281): S281 stays a row until this slice lands, then is retired as done by it. Carried from S281's findings (Wave 7, 2026-11-04): steering paused runs meant reading `run.json`, report files and the grok fixture directory under `~/.local/state/ork` by hand; `ork status` takes no run argument; it prints a paused run's long wait reason and every denied command on one line. S281 asked for the run state, the whole pause reason or owner question with its options, the latest report per role, the check results with their logs, and the denied commands as a count with the first few. This slice covers all of them; the fixture directory stays out (Q4). S176 (done) built `run.report`. S298 (shape pauses) points at this command. S247 (`ork projects show`) and S240 (status text clarity) are neighbors. S294 and S295 add pause kinds this command will show without change, because it prints `pending.reason` as stored.

sections.heading: Failing tests
sections.body:
In `internal/daemon/show_test.go`, with the run helper of `internal/daemon/report_test.go:20-31`:

- `TestRunShowReturnsThePauseInFull`: a run paused with kind `shape` and a 600 character reason. The reply holds `pending.kind`, `role`, `round` and the whole reason, unshortened and without the `; next:` suffix; plus the roles with report names, the `checks[]` rows with log names, and each finding with `text`. Fails first: no `run.show`.
- `TestRunShowNamesTheLatestReportOfThePendingRole`: records for `reviewer` attempts 1 to 3 and a `gate` role; pending role `reviewer` round 1. `latest_report` is `reviewer-1-attempt-3.md`. With no pending, it is the last role record that has a report.
- `TestRunShowIsNotFoundForAnUnknownOrBadRunID`: `unknown` and `../r1` give `not_found`; a record that cannot be read gives the `internal` error `run ID cannot be read: WHY` (as `openRun`, `runs.go:1422-1431`).
- `TestRunShowDoesNotWaitForTheRun`: a busy run answers at once (the same rule as `run.report`).
- `TestRunReportServesAListedCheckLog`: `checks-1.log` listed in `checks[].log` returns its text through `run.report`; an unlisted `checks-9.log`, `run.json`, a path and a link are `not_found`. Fails first: `.md` only.
- `TestRunReportCutsALongLogAtALineEnd`: a log over 64 KiB is cut at a line end with `(cut: over 64 KiB)`.

In `internal/cli/show_test.go`:

- `TestShowPrintsTheSummaryAndThePendingReport`: `ork show RUN` on a paused run prints the state, the full reason, the report list, the check list and the pending role's newest report text (owner decision 2026-11-05, Q2 paused-report). On a run that is not paused it prints the summary only and names the reports. A role with 5 denied commands shows `denied 5:` and the first 3 names.
- `TestShowNamePrintsOneReportOrOneLog`: `ork show RUN reviewer-1-attempt-3.md` prints that text and nothing else; `ork show RUN checks-2.log` the same for a log; an unknown name exits 1 with the message and the list of names that exist.
- `TestShowJSON`: `--json` prints the `run.show` reply; with a NAME it prints `{name,text}`.
- `TestShowQuestionPausePrintsTheOptions`: a pause of kind `question` prints the question, its numbered options and `Recommend`, and `next: ork answer RUN TEXT`.
- `TestShowTakesRunAndOptionalName`: no argument and three arguments exit 2 with `show takes RUN [NAME]`; `ork help` lists the command.

sections.heading: Implement
sections.body:
1. Tests first. Confirm each fails for the reason given.
2. Add `run.show` (read-only, no wait, store-backed like `run.report`). Reply: `id`, `item`, `state`, `reason`, `pending` (`kind`, `state`, `role`, `round`, `reason`, `question`, `ask`, `key`; no `note`), `roles[]` (`role`, `round`, `attempt` derived from the report name or the order, `exit`, `report`, `denied` as a count and the first 3 names of `DeniedCommands`, carried from S281), `checks[]` (the record's rows), `findings[]` (`n`, `kind`, `title`, `text`, `ask`, `answer`, `filed`) and `latest_report` (the pending role and round's newest attempt with a report, else the newest report). Build it from the stored record; reuse the `EngineFinding` and `EngineRole` shapes where they fit.
3. Let `run.report` accept a name that a `checks[].log` lists. Keep every guard of the existing reader: plain name, regular file, no link, plain text, 64 KiB bound (owner decision 2026-11-05, Q3 extend-run-report).
4. CLI `ork show RUN [NAME] [--json]`. Text with no NAME: a header line (`ID ITEM STATE`), the pause reason in full on its own lines, the question and options when kind is `question`, the next command (the same one status prints), the role attempts with their denied-command count and first 3, the checks, the findings with text, and when paused, the pending role's newest report under a `-- NAME --` rule. With NAME: the file text only. Exit 1 with the existing names listed when NAME is unknown.
5. Serve nothing else (owner decision 2026-11-05, Q4): no live tail, no `run.json`, no fixture directory.
6. After this slice lands, the owner retires S281 as done by it (Q1); the build does not change S281.
7. Keep `ork status` as it is (S240 owns its wording). Do not add flags to it.
8. Docs and CHANGELOG in the same diff. *Proposed* CHANGELOG line under `## Unreleased`: "`ork show RUN [NAME] [--json]` prints a run's state, the whole pause reason, its role reports, check results and findings, and with NAME one role report or check log, so a paused run can be read without opening the run directory (S297)." *Proposed* docs: a `run.show` row and the check-log names in `docs/design.md` beside `run.report`; `docs/state.md:16-17` says both files are served by `run.report`; `docs/guide.md` adds the command to the list and `ork show RUN` to the paused-run row.

sections.heading: Check
sections.body:
- `go -C WORKTREE test -count=1 ./internal/daemon ./internal/cli ./internal/engine -run 'Show|Report'`: all pass.
- `go -C WORKTREE test -race -count=1 ./...`, `go -C WORKTREE vet ./...`, `gofmt -l WORKTREE` (empty), `slicer check`, `adj lint`.
- Mutation: let `run.report` skip the `checks[].log` listing guard; `TestRunReportServesAListedCheckLog` (the unlisted case) goes red.
- Mutation: print `wait` (with the `; next:` suffix) instead of `pending.reason`; `TestRunShowReturnsThePauseInFull` goes red.
- Security: the new log path must not read outside the run directory; the tests above include a path and a link.
- [HUMAN CHECK] [AFTER LAND] On a run paused on report shape, `ork show RUN` from an agent session prints the whole reason and the refused report, and `ork show RUN checks-1.log` prints a check log, without reading `~/.local/state/ork`.

sections.body: One commit on the slice branch: "Add ork show: pause reason, role reports and check logs".

sections.heading: Open owner questions
sections.body: None open. The owner answered Q1 to Q4 on 2026-11-05 with the recommended options (retire-s281, paused-report, extend-run-report, reports-and-logs-only); the lead records the decisions.
